description: Agent Support Operations: submit support performance records with the service commitments they answer to: the commitments with their reference, the first response time and the resolution time they set in hours, the share of tickets each says meets its time as a percent and the credit or remedy the terms promise when a commitment is missed; each support ticket with its id, reference, reporting period, the moment opened, the moment of the first response and the moment resolved; each performance report with its id, period, the first response and resolution percentages it states and the credit or remedy it records. The signed report gives the commitments, the tickets and the reports, each reported percentage recomputed from the ticket records for its period, each period that misses a commitment against the credit or remedy the terms promise, and each period the ticket records cover against a report, and counts them, and names divergent support performance records: a response or resolution percentage that does not recompute from the ticket records, a commitment miss with no credit or remedy recorded where the terms promise one, and a reporting period quietly skipped; then a report for a period with no ticket records and a remedy recorded for a period that meets every commitment, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No tickets, no reports, no committed hours, or a ticket with no opening time to the minute leaves those points unverified. Periods match without case, punctuation or word order with quarters and month names folded, a ticket meets a measure when its moment falls within the committed hours of its opening, and percentages are recomputed to the tenth of a point. This reads a support operation’s own ticket records against its own stated commitments: wever_sla-evidence-check and wever_sla-credit-check read a service provider’s SLA evidence and credits from the buyer’s side, while the SLA check recomputes the operation’s reported service levels from its own tickets. Verdict support_sla_divergent, support_sla_partial, support_sla_unverified or support_sla_consistent. POST /api/support-sla-check. Reads the support records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads the records as supplied only: it answers no customer, sends no message and opens, closes or changes no ticket, which stay with the support team, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Support Operations reads support operation records: ticket logs, first response records, resolution records, escalation records, promise records, performance records, backlog records and the support summary, each against the queue record, the stated response commitments, the customer confirmations, the stated escalation triggers, what the records show happened, the stated service commitments, the ticket list or the records beneath it. The family’s ground is support work already done, read across the whole queue: the DiligenceOps support brief reads one support conversation and lists the promises made in it, and the Agent Feedback family reads the loop around feedback on work, while this family checks whether the support operation’s records hold together across tickets. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-support-operations-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-support-operations/.
